subject: DPA: snapshot removal & onshore deletion playbook — clarification
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@aurumcloud.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@aurumcloud.com, terry.cho@aurumcloud.com
Date: 2026-09-18T08:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on snapshot retention and certified removal (DPA Annex B)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal and infra teams reviewed the draft Annex B and had a couple of open items before we can sign:

1) Backups & snapshots: we need a clear playbook describing how and when customer snapshots are identified and fully deleted (including cross-region replicas). The clause in redlined Annex B states "delete on request within 30 days" but doesn't say how backups/snapshots are reconciled.

2) Evidence: our auditors expect a measurable evidence artifact (signed manifest or retention log) proving the erase action and the timestamp.

3) Lawful access carveout: please confirm if an onshore copy kept for legal hold would be excluded from the standard erase flow and how we'd document holds in the retention timeline.

Could you provide a short operational flow and an ETA for sample evidence (we only need a proof-of-concept manifest format to share with audit). We attached our redlines (Annex-B_DPA_redline_v2.pdf).

Appreciate it — Sophie

--
Sophie Martin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Aurum Cloud

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@aurumcloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-18T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot retention and certified removal (DPA Annex B)

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Marissa (legal) and Jonas (ops) to own the specifics. Quick answers up front, then we'll follow with a short playbook doc:

- Snapshot reconciliation: Redwood maintains a 3-tier store: primary, async replicas, and archival snapshots. Our erase flow targets primary and async replicas first; archival snapshots are tombstoned and scheduled for scrub within the erase window unless explicitly scoped out.

- Evidence: we can provide a signed deletion manifest containing resource IDs, deletion timestamps (ISO8601), operator-id (system account), and a SHA256 checksum of the manifest. That manifest can be exported as a PDF/JSON and stored with audit retention.

- Legal hold: holds are documented in our retention ledger; any object under hold is flagged and excluded from automated scrub. We can annotate manifests to reflect holds and include a hold-release timestamp when cleared.

Action items from our side: Jonas will draft the Snapshot-Erasure-Flow.docx with sequence steps (identify, reconcile replicas, tombstone, scrub, manifest). Marissa will propose a short contract sentence to add to Annex B about "manifest as evidence" and a one-line carveout for lawful holds. Expect a first pass by EOD 9/19.

Sound OK?

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@aurumcloud.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-19T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot retention and certified removal (DPA Annex B)

Hi Sophie — following up with proposed contract language and an operational note. I've attached a short flow doc. Highlights:

Contract proposal (suggested insertion to Annex B):
"Provider will, upon Customer request or at the expiration of the retention period, execute the deletion of customer data and any associated snapshots and replicas within the timeframe specified in this Agreement. Provider will produce a signed deletion manifest (manifest includes resource identifiers, deletion actions taken, and timestamps). Where data is subject to an active legal hold, Provider will not obliterate the data but will produce manifest entries documenting the hold and subsequent release."

Operational clarifications (non-contractual bullets):
- Identification: nightly reconciliation job identifies objects eligible for deletion and enumerates associated replicas across zones.
- Replica sync: deletions are cascaded; each cascade step emits an event recorded in the retention ledger.
- Archive handling: archived snapshots are flagged for a scrub window (default 60 days) to allow for hold reversals; this window is configurable in enterprise plans.

We propose a 30-day primary scrub commitment (operational target) and explicit language that archival scrub may take up to 60 days for safety; this matches many SOC-2 expectations while giving operational breathing room. If Aurum requires faster archival scrub, we'd like to understand the use-case and impact (cost/availability).

Please see the attached Snapshot-Erasure-Flow.docx for the step-by-step flow and an example manifest. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk through.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@aurumcloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: terry.cho@aurumcloud.com
Date: 2026-09-20T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot retention and certified removal (DPA Annex B)

Marissa/Priyom — this is super helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from legal + infra after reading the flow:

- The manifest format looks fine but our audit wants a machine-verifiable artifact (JSON manifest with signature) rather than only a PDF. Can you include a signed JSON manifest example where Redwood's system key signs the manifest payload?

- For the archival scrub window: Aurum's policy requires that archived snapshots of European customer data be purged within 45 days when requested. We expect Redwood to support region-specific scrub windows as a binding SLA point in Annex B.

- Onshore copies for legal hold: we don't plan to keep onshore copies, but our compliance team wants a playbook for how Redwood will flag and track such holds should they arise (we need the ledger schema sample).

Would you be able to: (a) provide a signed JSON manifest example, (b) confirm willingness to add a region-specific scrub SLA (EU: 45 days archival scrub) as a negotiated deal term, and (c) share the ledger schema stub? If you can get (a) and (c) by EOD 9/20 we can run with legal review and aim to finalize Annex B next week.

Thanks — Sophie

--
Sophie Martin
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Aurum Cloud

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@aurumcloud.com>, priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on snapshot retention and certified removal (DPA Annex B)

Sophie — quick ops note and commitments from Redwood:

1) Signed JSON manifest: yes. We've produced an example signed-manifest JSON (includes resource IDs, deletion actions, ISO timestamps, and an RSA-PSS signature using our system key). We'll convert the example to both signed JSON and a PDF render. Expect sample attachments in a follow-up email within 2 hours.

2) Region-specific archival SLA: we can commit to a negotiated SLA. For Aurum (EU-scoped customers) we will accept an archival scrub SLA of 45 days as a contract term for the deal AC-2026-0911. That will be explicit in Annex B redline. Operationally that maps to a per-region scrub scheduler that honors region flags on snapshot metadata.

3) Ledger schema stub: attached will be a 1-page ledger-schema.txt showing the fields we emit for each event (object_id, region_tag, event_type, actor, timestamp, hold_id optional). This is non-sensitive and suitable for your compliance review.

We appreciate the specificity — we'll attach the signed JSON and ledger stub shortly. If Marissa and Priyom sign off on the Annex-B redline language, we can exchange final DocuSign tomorrow.

-Jonas

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
